purpose: Security impact analysis (SIA) for every change, per SCN-CSO-EVA. Each question is answered yes or no in the PR body. A yes forces at least the question's outcome. A question whose triggers match the diff must be answered explicitly, and a no needs a one-line reason. Path triggers apply anywhere; line patterns apply only to non-comment lines in line_scan_paths (configuration and infrastructure), not in code or comments that merely name the same things. Adapted from the security impact analysis template in NIST SP 800-128 to this system.

recurring_categories.dependency-update: A version change of a dependency, action or tool already in use, adding no new package or service.
recurring_categories.vulnerability-remediation: A fix, mitigation or decision record for a known vulnerability, through the existing VDR process.
recurring_categories.evidence-refresh: Regenerating or re-publishing evidence the pipeline already produces, with no change to how it is produced.

questions.question: Does the change alter the system's FIPS 199 impact level or its FedRAMP certification class?
Does it add an external service or interconnection that would receive customer or federal data?
Does it change how customers or app users authenticate, or what customers must configure themselves?
Does it move system data into another authorization boundary, or out of this one?
Does it introduce, collect or generate privacy-impacting data (PII or PHI)?
Does it change the cloud provider the system runs on?
Does it add a component, service, feature or app to the boundary?
Does it remove a component, service, feature or app?
Does it add or change an external service, interconnection or third-party component (whatever data it handles)?
Does it add, remove or weaken a security control, gate or compensating control?
Does it change how compliance status is decided or published (gates, assessor, reconciliation, generators, rule statuses)?
Does it add or change a cryptographic module, key, algorithm, TLS setting or signing method?
Does it add or change an authentication mechanism or permissions for operators, CI or workloads (IAM, OIDC trust, workflow permissions)?
Does it add or change boundary protection or routing: ingress, egress, CloudFront behaviours, security headers, DNS or API routes?
Does it add, replace or remove monitoring, logging or alerting?
Does it change a scanning tool or its configuration (SCA, SAST, DAST, IaC scanning)?
Is it a major upgrade of an operating system, language runtime, policy engine or database?
Does it change how the pipeline builds, signs, publishes or deploys?
Does it change backup, retention or recovery?
Does it move the system or part of it to a new region or facility?
Does it change what data the system stores or processes, or a component's data sensitivity or classification?
